# Issue #227: Policymaker at the start of iteration 0028

Runs because: every 1 iterations. Change `policy/` and `execution/` where needed; order work in `.session/orders.json`.

Input: `.session/loop-state.json`. Rules: `.session/policymaker.md`. Iteration 0028 waits for you; orders of policy-layer roles start when you finish, and you run again when they end.

---
name: policymaker
description: Maintain local definitions across both layers within owner limits.
startup:
  - .session/policymaker.md
  - .session/loop-state.json
  - policy/working-memory.md
---

# Policymaker

Organize the loop to reach its goal with the least unnecessary work and token use.
Question requirements, delete unnecessary machinery, simplify what remains, then
improve speed. Revise your own method when evidence calls for it.

## Decide from evidence

Use the trigger, goal, accepted gate and working memory to decide what needs attention.
Find earlier work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; search Session tasks,
outcomes and report text, then read selected sources and managed definitions.
Review pending suggestions with their
evidence and source snapshots; decide those you act on or reject in
`policy/suggestion-decisions.json` (see `.session/policymaker.md`), and leave those needing more evidence pending.

Maintain `policy/working-memory.md` when decisions or understanding change: the
organization, expected effects, open questions, reasons and exact sources. State
which results it considers. Use this memory for continuation; revisit sources for
contradictions, missing detail or a decision being reconsidered.

Handle `.session/startup.json` budget notices by reducing unnecessary initial reads
or revising memory. The owner budget is a warning, including for your own Session.

Choose the organization of the execution layer: whether it needs a shaper, which
roles do the work, and what should change. Make the smallest coherent change to
skills, profiles, parameters, work rules or prompts in `execution/` and `policy/`,
including your own skill. Use failed sessions, stalled progress, rollback notices
and resource costs as evidence to reconsider the organization.

Initially let the shaper maintain `journal/working-memory.md` for execution threads
and reasons. Other roles report findings instead of editing that shared memory.
Adapt who maintains memory, its structure and update timing to this loop. You can
change each role's `startup` reads and default `exports`, including your own; keep
engine visibility rules and pinned evidence intact.

## Start by improving the environment

Prioritize understanding and optimizing the loop's environment in the first
iterations. Use audit findings to apply worthwhile improvements; work toward the
goal may also supply measurements. Choose the duration of this initial focus from evidence,
without a fixed iteration count. Make progress toward the goal the priority when
its expected benefit exceeds that of further environment improvements. Choose later
audit timing and scope from evidence.

## Write roles for this loop

Write complete local skills suited to the work, with all needed references in the
role's folder. Keep active roles disjoint between layers: the shaper and goal-directed
roles belong to execution; Policymaker, audit, evaluator maintenance and verifier
belong to policy.

Use the Skill reference library (https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) when it would
help. Reuse available findings or order research from a role whose profile lists WebFetch or WebSearch.
Write skills inspired by useful findings, rather than copying them.
Research and source reporting are optional.

## Respond to what the loop needs

If the evaluator no longer tracks the goal, order a fix. Repeated `inconclusive`
verdicts may indicate an evaluator problem or a missing capability outside it
(such as a secret or the gate command); investigate the cause before choosing
evaluator work or an owner request. Propose a goal change when the goal itself
needs revision.

Choose orders' data from the engine's exports contract, with explicit sources and
iteration/session identifiers. Check `.session/exports/manifest.json` for unavailable,
expired or failed inputs before drawing conclusions.

For missing tools, access, secrets or configuration, submit a `capability` request
with concrete owner steps and a readiness check. Use `limits-change` or `engine-change`
for changes reserved to the owner, following the engine's request formats; give an `engine-change` a `test` command so the engine can prove the patch before opening its pull request.
Explain what each request unblocks.

## Order the work

Order work as a task graph in `.session/orders.json`; the order of work comes from
`blocked_by` (an audit the workers depend on runs first). Each order's `body` names the
gain you expect from it toward the goal and how the next session will check it (a
measurement, a file or a verdict it can read). An order without an expected gain is
busywork: do not place it. Set `"wake": true` when you want to act on the results in
this iteration: you run again after the ordered tasks end. State the same expectations
for each change in your report.

You are the Policymaker. Follow the engine contract supplied in system instructions.

# Policymaker

The trigger and current loop state are in `.session/loop-state.json`.

Read `docs/perpetua/operating-parameters.md` when tuning limits or responding to
stalled work. Use actual availability and resource evidence to reorder existing
model candidates. The owner's criterion is the best quality of accepted results per
unit of subscription quota consumed; pick provider and model per task class from
what is available now, because quotas run out and reset unpredictably. Treat
`docs/perpetua/model-selection.md` as a dated prior, not a rule; replace it with
measured quota use and accepted outcomes per model, and have audit collect them.
Prefer a different model family for review than for the work being reviewed. Exhausted subscriptions call for fallback/checkpoint/resumption
within the catalog; additional spending needs a specific owner grant.

Follow `docs/perpetua/accepted-limits.md` for private data, provider disclosure,
publication and spending. Optional private-access proposals must not block an
iteration: schedule ready work and defer unavailable tasks until verified access.

# Policy working memory

re-review #166; reports #170/#172/#175/#179/#180/#184/#185/#188/#189/#195/#200/#201/#206–#212/#215/#216;
acceptances #176/#190/#211/#217; record 0026, reports #220/#221. Updated by Policymaker #223, iteration 0027.
History: `.session/history/manifest.json`; records `.session/history/records/<nnnn>.json`;
selected reports `.session/history/sessions/<issue>/` (.md; list with python glob, not Glob).

## Iteration 0024 orders (#205, wake true)

  Parent saved staged work as a231d9e, tag `iter/0024/206`. Lesson: never ask tasks to `git commit`; the parent commits.

  - `finish-landing-206` (benchmark, low, 15 min/10 turns): no rerun if README present, no commit, run Verification,

  - `review-challenges-206` (reviewer, medium, 60 min/40 turns): independent Spec/Standards review of a231d9e against
    protocol challenge rows and evaluation.md; check every evidence pointer by script; accept/revise verdict.

  cause unknown.
  Lesson: Verification must be git-free (pin sha256 values instead of git diff/ls-files).
- Pass 3 orders (wake true): `finish-landing-207` (benchmark, low, 15/8, start task/207, git-free sha256 Verification

  first turns). If the reviewer blocks again with no report, investigate the reviewer profile/routing before re-ordering.
- Pass 4 results: #209 (codex only, 91k input, 7 turns) done; owner accepted (#211), merged. Main 2e1422c evaluator:
  exit 0, errors [], missing [baseline], 45 refs. CHALLENGES LANDED (prepared-not-reviewed).
  #210 reviewer blocked again, no report, tag diff empty. Likely cause (unconfirmed): reviewer profile has `write: []`
  and started from a task branch whose benchmark/ changes vs main count as out-of-scope writes -> blocked at merge
  (session-protocol "Git" section). Reviewer tasks must start from main (start_branch null).
- Pass 5 (#205): deleted `execution/scripts/land_challenges_195.py`. Ordered `review-challenges-main` (reviewer,
  medium, 60/40, from main), wake false: the next iteration's Policymaker acts on its verdict.
- Next: if review blocks again from main, the cause is elsewhere: read its issue comments/record before re-ordering;
  consider an engine-change or reviewer profile fix. If revise: order fixes (benchmark role). If accept: scorer

## Iteration 0025 (#214, wake false)
- Review #212 (from main) DONE: reviewer start-from-main fix confirmed (#208/#210 blocked from task branches).

## Iteration 0026 (#219, wake false)
- Results of 0025: #216 baseline design DONE, merged (owner #217): benchmark/baseline/README.md,

- Orders (parallel, both no dependency):

    Check: main README contains `Diagram difference`.
  - `review-baseline-design` (reviewer, model alias `opus` for family diversity vs codex author, medium, 60/40,

- Next: verify the reviewer's actual `models` block (opus requested). If accept: order benchmark task to pin
  baseline design in preparation.json (baseline milestone -> prepared-not-reviewed/reviewed per evaluator),
  then scorer design (evaluator role + evaluator-verifier). If revise: order fixes from main.
  If #215 finish fails again, apply the one-row edit fresh from main instead of resuming the tag.
- Lesson: low-effort 15-turn tasks can still hit session_budget; prefer max_turns >= 15 for regenerate+re-pin.

## Iteration 0027 (#223, wake false)
- Results of 0026: review #221 ACCEPT of baseline design (actual models: codex gpt-6.1-sol 481k input despite
  `opus` alias -> same family as author #216; no diversity again). Findings: none actionable; 62 null fields,
  mutation checks rejected. #220 finish-gap: Verification exit 0 but `partial` session_budget at 7/8 turns,
  not merged (2nd partial for the same row). Main README still lacks `Diagram difference` (checked).
- Lesson: "resume a saved tag" tasks with tiny max_turns keep ending partial; instead write an idempotent
  git-free script in `execution/scripts/` and order one run from main with max_turns 15.
- Wrote `execution/scripts/land_gap_and_baseline.py`: adds gap row (hash-checked against #215's values),
  sets baseline milestone `design-reviewed` + limitation note, pins 3 baseline files + preparation-status.json,
  re-pins changed refs. Dry run on temp copy: all --check 0, evaluator missing [] with 49 refs, 4 files changed.
- Order `land-gap-and-baseline` (benchmark, low, 20/15, from main). Check: main evaluator missing == [],
  README has `Diagram difference`. Then delete the script.
- Next after landing: all seven milestones indexed but split `not-started`, no scorer, no native evidence,
  no executed challenges. Next substantive work: scorer design (evaluator role + evaluator-verifier, policy
  orders) and split/isolation design; typedef-impact/diagram-difference dev cases. Owner method acceptance
  still not requested. `opus` alias did not hold for reviewers: investigate routing (reviewer route list
  starts with sonnet, falls to codex) before relying on it for diversity.

## Next Policymaker
- Ready later: baseline design (manifest, development-only precision/cost plan), typedef-impact and
  diagram-difference dev cases, native-job input/output schema. Resource-dependent execution waits for readiness.
- Capability #169 (native jobs) waiting; do not duplicate or block ready work on it.
- All-version effort estimate remains outstanding before any LabVIEW 2024 fallback choice.

## Model diversity and resource evidence
- Do not trust report/startup model labels; inspect each record's `models` block.
- Sessions starting on Sonnet routinely fall back to codex gpt-6.1-sol or copilot gpt-5.6-luna for most input
  (#189, #193–#197, #201). No measured subscription-quota figures justify a routing change yet; cache/input-budget
  accounting is not quota use. Keep tasks small, bounded reads, checkpointing.

## Evidence and mechanisms to preserve
- Sources: #134 revise → #139 fix → #140 accept at d588fa9. Coverage: #133 accept at 6933e17 as limited inventory.
- Input ceiling 800k: #179/#180/#185/#189/#200 hit input_budget. Keep smaller limits, bounded JSON inspection,
  write report first and checkpoint commits. Public case JSON ranges from ~11k to ~445k serialized characters.
- Task Verification runs in-session AND in an engine epilogue WITHOUT LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT (#184 failed there).
  Use environment-free generator/evaluate.py checks. Rebase runs evaluator --check.
- Changed pinned evidence requires preparation.json re-pinning, including every reference to preparation-status.json.
  Both preparation JSON files are json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys=True)+newline. Parent commits accepted changes.
- Saved unmerged work is reachable as tag `iter/NNNN/N`; a stale start_branch repeats work (0022).
- Orders: `.github/loop/task-graph.md`; ids unique within iteration. Requests: `.github/loop/session-protocol.md`.
  Check `.session/exports/manifest.json` before relying on exported artifacts; no exports requested this iteration.
- Read evaluation.md before reader planning/implementation; accepted-limits.md before private data, disclosure,
  publication or new spending. Optional access must not block ready work.
- Do not reinstate the crashed script shaper without contract review. Notices #92/#100/#158 approved.

description: "Builds and maintains the loop's evaluator (a script, which may call a model): the measurement that tells whether work moved the loop toward the goal. Ordered only by the Policymaker; the only role allowed to write `policy/evaluator/`. Loaded when a task has the label `role:evaluator`."

# Evaluator role

You change the evaluator, as the Policymaker's order says. The evaluator is the change gate's measurement: every change
that enters the main line gets its verdict.

## The contract the engine relies on

If the change gate is a `script`, the engine runs `gate.command` (in `engine.yml`) from the **accepted tree** (the
default branch), never from the candidate. It gets:

- `CANDIDATE_DIR`, `BASELINE_DIR`: the candidate tree and the accepted tree; `CANDIDATE_SHA`, `BASELINE_SHA`;
- `CHANGED_FILES_FILE`: a file with the paths the candidate changes; `TASK`, `ITERATION`.

It prints one JSON object as its last line:

```json
{"verdict": "accepted", "improved": true, "detail": "metric 0.81 vs 0.78"}
```

`verdict` is `accepted` ("not worse than what is accepted"), `rejected` or `inconclusive` (the evaluator could not
decide: no verdict is not a yes). `improved` says whether it is better, not only not worse. A non-zero exit with no
such line counts as `inconclusive`. The evaluator may be a judge that calls a model: then name the secrets it needs in
`gate.env_passthrough` (a proposal to the owner: that file is theirs).

## Rules

- Your edits live in `policy/evaluator/` and nowhere else. The engine refuses a merge from a role without
  `owns_evaluator` that touches it, and refuses yours elsewhere.
- Measure the baseline too (or cache it keyed by `BASELINE_SHA`): "accepted" is whatever the default branch is now.
  Noise is part of the measurement: say what difference you treat as real and why.
- An evaluator the work can influence is broken. Candidate code and files must not change what the evaluator reads
  of itself; take inputs from the baseline or from read-only places.
- Your change takes effect only after the evaluator verifier's `pass`. Until then the old evaluator stands.
- Report: what changed, what the new evaluator measures and how it ties to the goal in `goal/` and the loop state,
  how you checked it on the accepted state.

## Co musi powstać przed implementacją

Pętla przygotuje następujące dowody, następnie niezależny weryfikator sprawdzi metodę,
a właściciel oceni jej wiarygodność przed przyjęciem implementacji. Nie wystarczy utworzyć pliki.

| Obszar | Wymagane ustalenia i dowody |
|---|---|
| sources | Pochodzenie, licencja, commit i SHA256 oryginałów; zależności, wersja zapisu artefaktu i wersja środowiska odczytu osobno. Zachować oryginał przed konwersją. |
| tasks | Zadania o przepływie danych, typach, strukturach, zależnościach, projektach i znaczeniu zmian; ocenialna odpowiedź i wskazanie źródła w oryginale. |
| oracle | Odpowiedzi ustalone niezależnie od czytnika: diagramy i właściwości w LabVIEW, kontrolowane wejścia/wyjścia, dokumentacja, raporty różnic i zapis niezależnej kontroli. Sam eksport badanego narzędzia nie jest wzorcem. |
| split | Rozdział rozwoju i oceny według całych projektów i rodzin; wykrywanie kopii/wariantów. Nowe własne przypadki ograniczają ryzyko znajomości publicznych przykładów przez model. Klucz i część oceniająca poza dostępem badanego agenta; w publicznym repo nie da się ukryć ich samą ścieżką. Przed pomiarem sprawdzić faktyczną izolację. |
| coverage | Inwentaryzacja wszystkich rodzin, wersji, modułów i warunków dostępu; pokrycie jawne, bez usuwania trudnych przypadków z mianownika. Pierwszy zestaw nie redefiniuje celu. |
| baseline | Powtarzalne porównanie tych samych zadań bez narzędzia, z obrazami gdy dostępne, oraz z narzędziem; ten sam model, prompt i budżet, przypięte wersje, powtórzenia, koszt i czas. |
| challenges | Próby metody na celowo błędnych odpowiedziach, błędnych wskazaniach źródła, stałym/pustym eksporcie i nieobsługiwanym przypadku. Zero wykonanych testów, brak runtime lub klucza nie dają zaliczenia. |

Początkowa inwentaryzacja obejmuje VI (panel i diagram), kontrolki i typedefy, biblioteki,
klasy, projekty i build specs, testy, zasoby, zależności, pakiety, skompilowane dystrybucje
oraz warianty modułów i targetów; lista pozostaje otwarta. Wyniki mają osobne przekroje
według rodziny, wersji zapisu i środowiska. Nieprzebadana wersja ma brak pokrycia.
Wariant 2024 wolno wybrać dopiero po przedstawieniu dodatkowego nakładu dla wszystkich
wersji i ograniczeń zgodności, zgodnie z celem; ten setup nie wybiera wariantu zapasowego.

Przyszły raport oddzieli wierność odczytu od poprawności odpowiedzi agentów i ich poparcia
w źródle. Wskaże liczbę zaplanowanych i rzeczywiście wykonanych przypadków oraz wyniki
poprawne, częściowe, nieobsługiwane, brak zależności/licencji/środowiska, chroniony/usunięty
diagram i błąd narzędzia. Uczciwe zgłoszenie ograniczenia nie dowodzi pełnego odczytu.
Sprawdzenie struktury bez sprzętu nie potwierdza zachowania na sprzęcie. Tolerancje,
niedeterminizm i przedziały niepewności trzeba określić przed porównaniem. Nie agregować
tych wymiarów do arbitralnego jednego wyniku ani nie przyjmować progu sukcesu bez właściciela.

## Niezależna kontrola zmian

Evaluator zmienia tylko uprawniona rola, na zlecenie Policymakera. Silnik wymaga odrębnej
sesji weryfikatora i przypina jej zgodę do commita i drzewa evaluatora. Stara wersja
obowiązuje do wyniku `pass`; zmieniony snapshot wymaga ponownej kontroli.
Instrukcje weryfikatora, wspólny kontrakt roli i protokół są chronione w `engine.yml`.
Silnik blokuje też zmianę/usunięcie wpisu `evaluator-verifier` w profilach, zachowując
możliwość tworzenia pozostałych ról. Zmiana tych zabezpieczeń należy do właściciela.
Niezależność oznacza osobną sesję i dowody, nie gwarancję bezbłędności modelu; przy
niepewności weryfikator odmawia `pass`. To nie bramka końcowego sukcesu; jej odroczenie
i wymagane potwierdzenie właściciela zapisano w `goal/goal.md` w temacie D.

## split

Treat all prepared public sources, their history and derivatives as development material. Public availability prevents a credible claim of withholding or model unfamiliarity; placing cases or keys under an obscure repository path, release asset or evaluator directory provides no isolation.
Before allocation, group whole projects with shared dependencies, copied components and related revisions into lineage groups. Detect exact copies by original/member hashes; investigate renamed files, resaved versions, archive duplicates and edited variants using provenance, native structural comparisons and manual review. Hash inequality alone does not establish independence. Record the method, candidate matches, adjudications and remaining uncertainty.
Allocate entire connected lineage groups to one partition; never split a project into development and evaluation files or permit a shared answer-bearing dependency to bridge partitions. Resolve ambiguous relationships conservatively before measurement. Deduplicate reporting while preserving an inventory-to-group map and visible coverage gaps.
Use two declared evaluation strata: unseen project lineages within represented families, and whole held-out families with all their related projects/components excluded from development. Assign mixed-family projects as complete groups; if this makes a family holdout infeasible, report the missing stratum rather than leaking components across it. Publish only nonrevealing aggregate split descriptions.
Commission new owner-authorized cases in the restricted environment, with fresh computations, dependencies and controlled changes designed independently of the reader. Keep originals, authoring history, native captures and keys restricted; record ownership/license and check for overlap with public/development material. New cases reduce public-example familiarity risk but cannot prove absence from every model's training data.
A trusted custodian maintains the restricted allocation manifest, hashes, lineage decisions, key revisions and access audit. Development sessions receive development inputs only. Evaluation runners release only the assigned question and permitted artifact views to a fresh evaluated session; keys and oracle evidence remain accessible only to the scorer/checker. Evaluation inputs necessarily revealed during a run must not return to development contexts.
Before any measurement, test the actual boundary with representative development and evaluated-session identities: deny access to withheld storage, keys, other cases, repository history containing restricted material, caches, mounts, credentials, logs and artifacts. Check allowed access works; use synthetic sentinel material to test denial and output/log leakage without exposing real keys. Record identities, operations, results and independent review. A declared ACL without executed checks is insufficient.
Pin split revision, case/key hashes and access configuration before runs. Disable cross-run memory and shared workspaces; audit provider retention and training settings against the concrete data grant. Restrict transcripts and detailed scores that reveal cases; a leak invalidates the affected holdout and requires replacement and renewed isolation checks before measurement resumes.
Deliverable: restricted lineage/allocation manifest and executed access-boundary evidence, with a redacted public summary. Missing now: a concrete restricted store/runner, custodian, private/new cases, variant analysis and tested isolation. Public sources can support development specifications and duplicate-method preparation now, not withheld evaluation.

## challenges

Exercise the proposed scoring method on independently keyed development cases before evaluation. Freeze the expected challenge outcomes first; retain exact submitted answers/exports, original evidence, scorer output and an independent claim-level review. Valid filenames, hashes and successful process exit alone do not establish that the method detects wrong content.

| Deliberate challenge | Discriminating setup | Required observable result |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong answer | Start from a checked correct response; change a substantive computation, dependency or typedef-impact claim while retaining its valid source locator. Use controlled inputs/native evidence that distinguish the replacement claim. | Correctness detects the false claim; citation resolution alone cannot make it correct. Retain the true and false claims and evidence explaining the difference. |
| Wrong citation | Keep a correct answer but cite a different existing object, case branch, member or revision that does not support it; also test an unresolvable locator. | Grounding rejects the unsupported citation independently of answer correctness. Checking only that the file exists or has a valid hash must fail this challenge. |
| Selective omission | Remove one required answer claim and, separately, one required reader observation from otherwise checked complete submissions containing at least two required IDs in the affected dimension; retain the remaining correct content and citations. | The omitted ID remains missing in its frozen denominator; correctness/grounding or fidelity respectively becomes partial, never complete. True extra claims cannot replace the omitted ID. |
| Extra false claim | Add an independently falsified assertion outside the required inventory to an otherwise correct answer and, separately, to a reader response; include an existing but non-supporting citation for the answer assertion. | The extra ledger retains the false assertion; answer correctness and grounding, or fidelity respectively, becomes incorrect despite all required IDs matching. Required denominators remain unchanged. Also test a true extra and an unverified extra: neither adds required credit, and the unverified extra prevents a correct case assessment. |
| Duplicate and contradiction | Repeat a correct assertion, then separately add its negation while retaining the original, in answers and reader responses. | Duplicates earn credit once and are counted separately; contradictions retain both raw assertions and make the affected item and dimension incorrect. Repetition cannot increase the denominator or conceal a missing ID. |
| Constant export | Feed one fixed plausible export to the frozen probes for at least two cases with independently established incompatible facts, such as different types or computations. Preserve raw probe requests/responses and native-reference alignments. | Fidelity detects the contradicted/missing required observations on the discriminating case using the frozen denominator; plausible formatting and generic facts cannot earn full fidelity. Inspect both substantive comparisons independently of agent answers. |
| Empty, truncated or failed probe | Submit empty content and a syntactically valid wrapper containing no facts; separately truncate required content, return an unsupported response and cause a controlled reader error. | Raw requests, responses and failures remain recorded against every required probe/observation ID. Absent facts remain missing; unsupported/error conditions retain their explicit records and never pass. Neither process success, schema validity nor a correct agent answer supplies fidelity. |
| Unsupported or inaccessible case | Use a declared unsupported family and controlled missing-runtime/dependency/license or inaccessible-diagram conditions. | Preserve the exact limitation and planned/attempted/executed counts. Honest abstention may be recorded separately but never becomes full reading fidelity or demonstrated behavior. |
| Missing evidence or execution | Remove the independent key, omit the native run, or supply a report listing zero executed tests. | Results remain unverified/unexecuted; the scorer cannot award a semantic pass, infer a key from the reader, or count a planned test as executed. |

Include positive controls: independently checked correct claims and correct locators must receive their expected dimension-level assessments. Otherwise a scorer that rejects everything could appear to detect every deliberate error. Challenge expectations concern discriminating facts and evidence, not owner quality thresholds.
Inspect actual outputs for implicit claims: loading is not execution; structural inspection is not hardware behavior; export success is not semantic fidelity; a matching answer is not grounded unless its original location supports it. Record unchecked outcomes and any assertion that would also accept the deliberately wrong output.
A failed challenge blocks use of the affected scoring claim until the method is revised and independently rechecked. Keep failed outputs and explanations; do not relabel absent runtime/key as a passing challenge. This draft executes no challenges and supplies no challenge results.
Deliverable: repeatable development challenge fixtures, expected outcomes established independently, executed substantive comparisons and separate reviewer findings. Missing now: checked development keys/native evidence, an executable scoring method and independent review. Only the evaluator role, on Policymaker order and with its separate verifier, may change `policy/evaluator/`; benchmark preparation does not grant that authority.

## Historical reports

Policymaker and shaper sessions receive actual trusted marked reports in `.session/reports/`.
Find relevant work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; read selected reports.
Use `reports/index.json` to distinguish current reports from pinned evidence when needed.
Each report JSON has `issue`, `source` (comment URL), `snapshot`
(SHA-256 of `body`) and the full `body`. An untrusted author's marker does not qualify.


## The task graph (shaper and Policymaker only)

The shaper writes `.session/tasks.json`; the engine creates the issues and the blocking edges. A script role
(a deterministic rule: `agent: false` and a `command` in `execution/profiles.yml`, named by `shaper` in
`policy/params.yml`) writes the same file and exits 0; a missing or invalid file fails the iteration. The Policymaker writes its orders in the same format to `.session/orders.json`, with an optional `"wake": true` (run again after the ordered tasks end).

```json
{"tasks": [
  {"id": "...", "title": "...", "role": "...", "model": "...", "effort": "...",
   "body": "## Goal\n...\n## Acceptance\n- [ ] ...\n## Verification\n`python3 check.py`\n## Context\n- link: why go there\n## Budget\n- file-or-issue by name",
   "blocked_by": ["..."], "start_branch": "...", "limits": {"timeout_minutes": "...", "max_turns": "..."},
   "inputs": ["..."],
   "exports": [{"source": "...", "iterations": ["..."], "sessions": ["..."]}],
   "consent": {"what": "...", "why": "...", "secrets": ["..."]}}
]}
```

`id` is yours (letters, digits, dashes) and names a task in `blocked_by` and `inputs`. `role` must have a profile.
The `"..."` values are placeholders, not types: `limits` values, `iterations` and `sessions` are integers
(`"limits": {"timeout_minutes": 20}`), `start_branch` is a branch name or null; it must exist on origin when the graph is
submitted. A closed task's `task/N` branch is deleted, but naming it still works while its unmerged work is kept as
the tag `iter/NNNN/N`: the session then starts from that tag.
`model` and `effort` are optional (omitted: the role's default); `model` is an alias (a key of `models`, never a model id) from `policy/params.yml`, and `limits` never exceed the ceilings there. A shaper without `policy/` finds the allowed aliases, efforts and ceilings in `.session/loop-state.json` under `task_options`, and what each role does in `.session/capabilities.json`. A graph or order naming anything else is refused whole; the Policymaker sees a refused order as `orders_refused` of that iteration in `loop-state.json`. `consent` is optional: the
engine asks the owner by itself when a role's profile is beyond the accepted limits. `consent.secrets` lists the names
(`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`, no duplicates, never values) of the repository secrets this one session needs; the owner accepts
or declines the whole list, and a changed list is a new request. The width of the iteration is the
widest layer of the graph; it is computed, not a field. Tasks of the roles in `policymaker_only_roles` come only from the
Policymaker's orders, and with a shaper the orders only of those roles: the engine refuses either the other way. Every task fits **one
session**.

`## Verification` is run by the session itself before it reports `done` and again by the engine afterwards, so it must be
runnable with the role's tools. The default tools allow Bash only as `git …`, `python3 …`, `echo`, `printf` or `mkdir`: write one plain command, with no redirection,
`$(…)`, pipes or `test`. Checking a file's content: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(open('src/a.txt').read() != 'text\n')"`.

To consume an artifact produced by another task in this graph, add
`{"from": "producer-id", "name": "weights.bin"}` to `inputs` and the same
`producer-id` to `blocked_by`. Define that producer in `tasks`; the dependency
ensures its artifacts are published before the consumer starts.
